newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to release Cyprus-registered ship.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to release Cyprus-registered ship.

text.p: Sri Lanka will release a Cyprus-registered freighter and its 28 Cuban crew members detained by the navy off the northeastern coast, a navy spokesman said on Tuesday.
"We searched the ship after she was detained because she was making suspicious movements," he told Reuters. "Nothing suspicious was found and we're going to release her."
The spokesman said the 1,674 tonne Caribbean Queen was detained after she refused to answer calls on radio and ignored warning shots fired by air force planes in waters off a major rebel stronghold.
"We had intelligence that there was a suspicious ship off Mullaitivu (on the east coast) that could be unloading arms for the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam)," he said.

The navy spokesman said he could not immediately say how the crew had explained their actions. The Cuban ambassador was flown to Trincomalee, where the ship was detained, but embassy officials refused to comment on the incident.
A Defence Ministry statement said on Monday that the ship was fired at and forced to stop for a search and identification when it suddenly started her engine and tried to sail away.
